evidence.observation: Spread 3: "BIRD!" shouted Jo. A sparrow fluttered from the fence. Nora frowned. "Now we'll never see anything." Jo's shoulders drooped.
Spread 4: Mama said, "You hoped for a butterfly. Jo hoped to help. That's two big hopes." Nora's tight hands opened a little.
Spread 5: The garden path curved toward the creek. Mama whispered, "What can we notice without chasing or touching?" Nora made up a rule: "Eyes look, ears hear, gentle hands stay near."

Spread 7: Scritch-scratch came from a fallen log beside the stone. A pill bug curled into a tiny gray ball when the log trembled. Nora and Jo stepped back. Soon it uncurled. Box two got a dotty circle.

Spread 8: "My turn to notice?" Jo whispered. Nora remembered his droopy shoulders. She scooted over. "Your turn." Together they said, "Eyes look, ears hear, gentle hands stay near." Jo pointed—not too close—to three ants carrying crumbs.
Spread 10: One box was still empty. "What else can we notice?" Nora asked Jo. The sky turned from bright to dim. A cool puff brushed their cheeks. Leaves flipped their pale undersides.

Spread 11: "Rain is coming!" Jo said. Plink! One drop landed inside box four. Plink-plink! Nora laughed. "The rain noticed my notebook!" They hurried home together—no butterfly, but four true surprises.
